prompt: The polynomial $p$ is defined by $p(x) = x^3 - 4x$. Which of the following is a factor of $p(x)$?

hints.text: $x^3 - 4x = x(x^2 - 4)$, and $x^2 - 4$ is a difference of squares.

learningObjective: Factor a cubic by extracting a common term and a difference of squares.
explanation: The remaining factor is a difference of squares: $x^2 - 4 = (x + 2)(x - 2)$.
So $p(x) = x(x + 2)(x - 2)$, and $x - 2$ appears among the factors.

alternativeExplanations.title: Test each candidate with the Factor Theorem
steps: $(x - a)$ is a factor exactly when $p(a) = 0$.
Test $a = 4$: $p(4) = 64 - 16 = 48 \neq 0$ ✗. Substituting is often faster than factoring when the choices are handed to you.
